newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK seen earning HK$85 billion from tourism in 1996.
newsitem.headline: HK seen earning HK$85 billion from tourism in 1996.

text.p: The British colony of Hong Kong is expected to earn a record HK$85 billion (US$11 billion) from tourism in 1996, the Hong Kong Tourist Association (HKTA) said on Thursday.
The HKTA said tourism receipts in the first half of 1996 rose 17.6 percent on the year to HK$40.9 billion.
"The HKTA is foreasting a year-end increase in total tourism receipts of some 13 percent to around HK$85 billion," a record figure," the HKTA said in a statement.
The British colony earned HK$75 billion from tourism in 1995.
Vistors from North Asia were the biggest spenders during the six-month period with a total of HK$9.3 billion, followed by tourists from China with a total of HK$7.9 billion, the HKTA said.
